title: Decompose legacy scenario driver and modernize perf-regression pipeline
creator: Samira Patel
description:
Problem:
The current end-to-end benchmarking harness is a single large Python driver that mixes scenario orchestration, load generation, metric aggregation, and CI gating. It's brittle (flake-prone), hard to extend for new kernels/quantized builds, and slows down adding new regression scenarios. We've accumulated band-aid fixes and ad-hoc patches that make it difficult to validate perf changes safely for runtime and kernel upgrades.

Goal:
Refactor the harness into a modular driver + runner + aggregator architecture, introduce a lightweight scenario spec v2 (more declarative), upgrade critical dependencies (pytest, locust->custom runner shim, opentelemetry exporter), and add a deterministic perf-regression CI job that fails on statistically-significant regressions. Reduce time-to-add-new-scenario from days to hours and cut flakiness in CI perf runs by 50%.

Acceptance criteria:
- New harness split checked into repo under infra/perf/harness with clear README and runbook.
- Scenario spec v2 schema documented in Confluence and has at least 10 migrated scenarios (load, chat-streaming, embeddings).
- CI job perf-regression/weekly runs with stable baselines (S3-hosted) and threshold rules; PRs that regress >5% median latency or >8% p95 for two consecutive runs get flagged.
- Replace ad-hoc metrics postprocessor with otel-exporter -> metrics pipeline used by perf dashboards (grafana link in attachments).
- Rollout plan and rollback steps documented; migration scripts for existing scenarios included.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design & spec (2 days): finalize scenario v2 fields, runner interface, aggregation contract; design doc: https://confluence.internal.redwood/infra/perf/harness-v2
2) Core decomposition (4 days): extract driver loop into infra/perf/harness/driver, implement runner adapter interface and a lightweight in-process runner to replace locust dependency for controlled CI.
3) Metrics/aggregation (2 days): implement otel exporter and connector to our perf-metrics S3 buckets; update dashboards.
4) CI integration (3 days): add perf-regression workflow, baseline storage, result validator and gating step.
5) Migration & stabilization (ongoing): migrate 10 high-value scenarios, run 3 full baseline cycles, tune thresholds.

Risks & mitigations:
- Flaky network impact on CI baselines: run each baseline 3x across different worker pools and use median.
- Runner behavioral drift vs production: keep a compatibility mode that exercises the same kernel paths as prod runtime; compare token distributions.
- Longer-than-expected migration: prioritize scenarios that cover kernel/quantization critical paths first.

Rollout strategy:
- Feature-flag the new harness and land in canary branch.
- Run side-by-side weekly baselines for 2 weeks.
- Gradually move nightly perf jobs to harness-v2 once stability metrics satisfied (>50% flakiness reduction).

Telemetry & observability:
- Export per-run histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99) plus token throughput, GPU utilization, and memory footprints.
- Push job-level metadata to perf-dashboard taggable by PR and runtime build.

Migration checklist:
- [ ] Create harness-v2 branch and initial driver scaffold.
- [ ] Implement runner adapter and in-process runner shim.
- [ ] Implement otel exporter and verify with sample scenario.
- [ ] Add initial CI workflow and baseline storage.
- [ ] Migrate 10 scenarios and run 3 baseline cycles.
- [ ] Update runbook and internal doc links.

2025-11-13 - Marcus Liu: Did a quick spike on in-process runner feasibility. Found locust upgrade causes non-determinism in our env; abandoning locust for CI makes sense. Notes: https://gist.github.com/marcusliu/harness-spike
2025-11-14 - Priya Nair (review): Suggested adding otel to align with infra metrics; flagged need for gating on token distribution to avoid false regressions.

2025-11-16 - Marcus Liu: POC branch created: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-perf/compare/harness-v2 (PR: #4123). Initial driver/runner split and simple aggregator implemented. Running internal smoke runs.

2025-11-18 - Reliability eng sync: Agreed on baseline storage in s3://perf-baselines/runtime-1.20/ and threshold rules. Action: add validator script to fail PRs when regression exceeds thresholds for two consecutive runs.
2025-11-20 - QA: Began migrating chat-streaming scenarios (3/10 migrated). Observed p95 variance drop ~28% in preliminary runs. Will continue migration and run full weekly baselines.
